title: OpenAI Buys 10,000+ Macs to Train AI Agents
blurb: OpenAI and other AI labs are quietly snapping up thousands of Mac Minis and Mac Studios to train computer-use agents at scale.
body:
For two years, the narrative was that Apple had lost the AI race. The reality looks different: Apple spent the last decade building exactly the hardware AI labs now need most.

Why Macs?

  • Computer-use agents need a real OS to click, type, fail, and reset inside — not a simulation.
  • Mac Minis and Mac Studios offer dense, power-efficient compute that's cheap to rack at scale.
  • Apple Silicon's unified memory architecture is well suited to running many parallel agent instances.

OpenAI and other labs are reportedly buying 10,000+ of these machines specifically to generate training data from agents learning to operate real desktop environments.

The twist: Apple didn't set out to become critical AI infrastructure — it became one almost by accident, simply by building efficient, scalable personal computers for a decade.

SOURCE · Linas Beliūnas, LinkedIn
